abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus is sustained by dysfunctional Th cells that amplify autoreactive B-cell responses. Iberdomide, a cereblon modulator that degrades Ikaros and Aiolos, has shown clinical activity in lupus, yet its T cell-centric mechanism remains incompletely defined. Here, using purified Th cells and a PBMC-based T-B cell activation assay, we asked whether targeted degradation of Ikaros reprograms pathogenic T-cell circuitry and constrains B-cell hyperactivity. At baseline, lupus Th cells exhibited the canonical pattern of diminished IL-2 and TNF-α levels, with enrichment of Th2-associated cytokines and elevated IL-6 and IL-9 levels. Iberdomide restored IL-2 and TNF-α and suppressed Th2-associated cytokines, IL-6, and IL-9 across secreted and single-cell readouts. Although the relative frequency of CXCR5+PD-1+ Tfh-like cells increased, ICOS expression decreased; IL-21 increased numerically but not significantly in total CD4 T cells. In the PBMC-based T-B cell activation assay, iberdomide reduced B-cell recovery, plasmablast-like differentiation, and anti-dsDNA levels. Interdonor variability in cytokine modulation tracked more strongly with Ikaros than Aiolos. These findings show iberdomide alters lupus T-cell cytokine networks and is associated with reduced B-cell responses.

summary: Iberdomide degrades Ikaros in lupus Th cells, normalizing IL-2, TNF-α, and Th2/IL-6/IL-9 cytokines and reducing B-cell responses in a PBMC assay.
title: Ikaros degradation by Iberdomide correlates with normalization of cytokines in Th cells of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
